gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a rear camera needs its own 8 MP sensor to record 4K (3840 × 2160 is 8.29 million pixels), or names an under-$250 kit with Sony's IMX678 at both ends and what each channel writes when both record: the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K, where DashCamTalk's TonyM measured 24.6 Mbps front and 23.8 Mbps rear in H.265, 30 fps each.
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (both pages), roadgearlab.com, the-gadgeteer.com, digitalcameraworld.com and knowledgelib.io; caranddriver.com blocked the fetch and was not read. roadgearlab (cited) already has the principle for front cameras: IMX678 is 8.29 MP effective, the 5 MP IMX675 fits 2K natively, and cheap '4K' cams upscale. knowledgelib (cited) already says the Miofive S1 Ultra's rear ships set to 1440p and runs 25 fps. None applies the pixel count to the rear camera, none lists the Vantrue S1 Pro Max, and none gives a dual-4K kit's per-channel bitrate with both cameras recording. Productbible's only dual-4K rows (VIOFO A229 Ultra $299.99, BlackVue Elite 10 $589.99) are over budget. The principle is partly covered; the rear-sensor application and the measured dual-channel figures are new.
decides: It splits the question the way ChatGPT's own follow-up does. If the shopper means 4K on both cameras, only a kit with an 8 MP rear sensor qualifies: the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K has IMX678 front and rear (DashCamTalk), and the brief's partner table has it at $239.99 on vantrue.com (awin:vantrue, no record yet; I could not open Vantrue's page, it returned HTTP 429 five times). The trade-off is data rate: TonyM's 24.6 Mbps front is about 0.43 of the roughly 57 Mbps roadgearlab lists for the VIOFO A229 Pro front (different testers and conditions). If '4K front and rear' means a 4K front with a rear camera, the VIOFO A229 Pro, DDPAI N5 Pro and DDPAI Z90 Pro are all 4K front plus 2K/1440p rear, so our two DDPAI rows belong on the page as 4K-front kits and must not be called 4K rear. VIOFO's own store returned 349.99 for the A229 Pro 2CH today through the store tool, which shows no currency; if that is USD it is over budget at the maker's store and needs another seller's price.
